assessment: The incumbent already provides usable course sets in 32/40 exports, and unchanged-assignment centers have a seven-minute median: evidence against assuming a universal workflow failure. Assignment changes and renames concentrate the observed exceptions but do not establish causes. D1-O5 limits a computation-speed explanation: replacement waits greatly exceed job duration. Zero sampled cross-center rows does not establish isolation, especially with the split-course center absent. Spreadsheet actions and timetable accuracy remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for a requested historical week may exclude intended courses after reassignment.
openings.delta: Test requested-week membership before changing export scheduling or generation speed.
openings.prediction: With attendance and course identity fixed, changing only the current assignment changes incumbent historical-week membership; an explicit week-specific selection restores the expected courses.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare unchanged, midweek-reassigned, and postweek-reassigned courses against a stipulated expected set. Prototype authorized, center-scoped week selection only if the mismatch reproduces. Retain the CSV schema; test concurrent attendance entry and same-named courses across centers. Bound work to six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Assignment affects export membership, not merely displayed information.
Week-specific membership can be recovered or explicitly selected within the available budget; otherwise the prototype remains diagnostic.

openings.claim: Do renamed courses produce missing participant rows, or complete files that coordinators mistake for omissions when matching timetable names?
openings.delta: Distinguishes data omission from recognition and reconciliation work requiring different remedies.
openings.prediction: If recognition drives the rename exceptions, fabricated rows remain complete and an internal old-name/new-name mapping reduces false omission reports; true missing rows persist despite that mapping.
openings.probe: Use the six coordinators in two short sessions with fabricated renamed-course exports: inspect completeness against known course identities, then compare matching and import actions with and without a private name mapping. Record checking, correction, download, and import time separately; preserve the documented CSV.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate the relevant reconciliation behavior.
A name mapping can be shown inside authorized workspaces within the shared six-day budget.
